body:
Travis Green signed a multiyear contract through the 2030-31 season with the Ottawa Senators on Monday.

The 55-year-old was hired as Senators coach May 7, 2024, and has guided them to the Stanley Cup Playoffs in each of his first two seasons.

“It means a lot, as far as the job, the city, what you're looking for I think as a coach, because it's not always the same in every organization,” Green said. “Every organization is run a little different, I think, but as coaches, you're always looking for something that works for you. 

“You know, words like stability, commitment, collaboration … I think you know when you talk about stability (that) we have that with our organization.”

Ottawa has won six of its first nine games (6-3-0) this season despite trading former captain <forge-entity title="Brady Tkachuk" slug="brady-tkachuk-8480801" code="player">Brady Tkachuk</forge-entity> to the Florida Panthers on June 21. The Senators host the Panthers on Wednesday (7:30 p.m. ET; Prime, SCRIPPS).

“It's an exciting day for our organization,” general manager Steve Staios said. “This became a priority for me as I watched our group continue to develop and watch the work of not only Travis, but the entire coaching staff and the collaboration and the way that they've been able to continually grow with this group. I think about the qualities of Travis when I first identified, went through the process, and he's been able to deliver on all of those, so it's a proud day for me. It's a proud day for the organization. I think we both understand that we have a lot of work ahead of us, but again, this is another foundational step for us and the Ottawa Senators moving forward.

“When situations get harder, he seems to rise to the occasion, and those are all qualities in great leadership, period. Not just in coaching. The lines of communication, the trust, I know the players, they believe, and I believe that Travis really cares for these players. And it's a tough situation to be in as a coach because you’ve got to hold them accountable. But he's got a great balance of being able to do both."

Several members of Green's staff, including assistants Nolan Baumgartner, Ben Sexton, Mike Yeo and goaltending coach Justin Peters, also signed new contracts Monday.

“I love living here,” Green said. “I love the city. I love the team, and I want to win. So, for me, it was an easy decision.”

*NHL.com independent correspondent Zoe Pierce contributed to this report*
